1.word_for_word: अष्ट-चत्वारिंशकेऽथ कृष्णः कुब्जाम् अरीरमत् । — In the eighth and forty-eighth century, Lord Kṛṣṇa attacked the hunchback.; अक्रूरस्य गृहं गत्वा तं गजाह्वयम् आदिशत् ॥ — He went to Akrūra’s house and ordered him to call Gaja.; सैरन्ध्री-कामम् आपूर्य पूरयित्वा मनोरथान् । — Sairandhri’s desires were fulfilled and she fulfilled her desires.; अक्रूरस्य ततः कृष्णस् तेन पार्थानसान्त्वयत् ॥१॥ — Then Krishna consoled the Partha with Akrura's words.
1.translation: In the eighth and forty-eighth century, Lord Kṛṣṇa attacked the hunchback. He went to Akrūra’s house and ordered him to call Gaja. Sairandhri’s desires were fulfilled and she fulfilled her desires. Then Krishna consoled the Partha with Akrura's words.

2.word_for_word: महार्हैर् अनर्घ्यैर् उपस्कारैर् गृहोपकरणैर् अन्वितम् । — It was accompanied by expensive and inexpensive gifts and household items.; कामोपायैस् तद् उद्दीपकैः सुरत-बन्धादि-लेख्यैर् उपबृंहितम् ॥२॥ — It is enhanced by the means of lust, by the stimuli, by the writings of pleasure, bondage and so on.
2.translation: It was accompanied by expensive and inexpensive gifts and household items. It is enhanced by the means of lust, by the stimuli, by the writings of pleasure, bondage and so on.

5.word_for_word: प्रसाधितो योग्यतमापादित आत्मा देहो यया सा । — The soul, which has been processed and attained to the most worthy, is the body by which it is attained.; स-व्रीडं यल् लीलया उद्गतं स्मितं, तद् येषु विभ्रमेषु तद्-युक्तैर् ईक्षितैर् उपलक्षिता ॥५॥ — The smile that playfully emerged with shyness was noticed by those who looked at her in the midst of her delusions
5.translation: The soul, which has been processed and attained to the most worthy, is the body by which it is attained. The smile that playfully emerged with shyness was noticed by those who looked at her in the midst of her delusions

6.word_for_word: अनुलेपार्पणाद् अन्यत् तस्याः पुण्यं नास्तीति दर्शयितुं पुण्य-लेशयेत्य् उक्तं न तु पुण्यस्याल्पत्व-विवक्षया ॥६॥ — To show that there is no merit for her other than offering ointment, it is said that she has a trace of merit, not to describe the insignificance of merit.
6.translation: To show that there is no merit for her other than offering ointment, it is said that she has a trace of merit, not to describe the insignificance of merit.

7.word_for_word: कुचादीनां रुजो मृजन्ती । — Wiping the pain of the breasts and other parts of the body.; जिघ्रन्ती च चरणम् ॥७॥ — and smelling the feet.
7.translation: Wiping the pain of the breasts and other parts of the body. and smelling the feet.

8.word_for_word: कामम् एव प्राकृत-दृष्ट्या अयाचत । — He asked for desire from a natural point of view.; न च गोप्य इव सा तन् निष्ठेति दुर्भगेत्य् उक्तम् । — It is said that she is not as unfortunate as the gopīs who are faithful to him.; कृतार्थत्वे तु तस्या न सन्देहः ॥८॥ — There is no doubt that she has been fulfilled.
8.translation: He asked for desire from a natural point of view. It is said that she is not as unfortunate as the gopīs who are faithful to him. There is no doubt that she has been fulfilled.

10.word_for_word: काम एव वरस् तं दत्त्वा । — Desire is the gift that gives him.; मानयित्वा चालङ्कारादि-दानैः ॥१०॥ — honoring him with ornaments and other gifts.
10.translation: Desire is the gift that gives him. honoring him with ornaments and other gifts.

11.word_for_word: मनो-ग्राह्यं विषय-सुखम् । — The pleasure of objects that is perceived by the mind.; असत्त्वात् तुच्छत्वात् ॥११॥ — Because of its non-existence and insignificance.
11.translation: The pleasure of objects that is perceived by the mind. Because of its non-existence and insignificance.

12.word_for_word: किञ्चिच् चिकीर्षयन् । — Wanting to do something.; हस्तिनापुर-प्रस्थापनं कारैतुम् इच्छन्न् इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that he wanted to send him to Hastinapur.; अक्रूर-प्रिय-काम्यया च ॥१२॥ — and by the desire to please Akrura.
12.translation: Wanting to do something. This means that he wanted to send him to Hastinapur. and by the desire to please Akrura.

13.word_for_word: आराद् दूराद् एव ॥१३॥ — From the distance of the arad.
13.translation: From the distance of the arad.

15.word_for_word: आ अप इति च्छेदः । — Aa up is the cut.; अप आ सर्वतो धारयन्न् इत्य् अन्वयः ॥१५॥ — They hold the waters from all sides, i.e., the waters.
15.translation: Aa up is the cut. They hold the waters from all sides, i.e., the waters.

17.word_for_word: वां युवयोर् इदं कुलम् उद्धृतं समेधितं च ॥१७॥ — This family of you and you has been raised and enriched.
17.translation: This family of you and you has been raised and enriched.

18.word_for_word: वाम् इदं कुलम् इत्य्-आदि-व्यवहार-दृष्ट्योक्त्वा परमार्थम् आह---युवाम् इति । — From the point of view of the behavior of saying, “This is your family,” he says the ultimate meaning: you.; जगन्-मयौ युवाम् । — You’re in the universe.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; जगद्-धेतू । — Jagad-dhetu.; तद् अपि कुतः ? — Where is that, too?; प्रधान-पुरुषौ तद् आत्मकौ अतो भवद्भ्यां विना परं कारणम् अपरं कार्यं च नास्तीति ॥१८॥ — The two primary Persons are that Self; therefore without You there is no other cause and no other cause.
18.translation: From the point of view of the behavior of saying, “This is your family,” he says the ultimate meaning: you. You’re in the universe. Where is it from? Jagad-dhetu. Where is that, too? The two primary Persons are that Self; therefore without You there is no other cause and no other cause.

19.word_for_word: ननु प्रत्यक्षादि-सिद्धं कथं नास्तीत्य् उच्यतेऽत आह---आत्म-सृष्टम् इति । — If so, how can it be said that there is nothing perfected by direct perception and other things?; हे ब्रह्मन् परमेश्वर । — O Brahman God.; "ब्रह्म" इति व पाठः । — "Brahma" is the v text.; रज-आदि-स्व-शक्तिभिर् आत्मनैव सृष्टम् इदं विश्वम् अन्वाविश्य कारणत्वाद् अननुप्रविष्टोऽप्य् अनुप्रविश्येव स्थितः श्रुत-प्रत्यक्ष-गोचरं यथा भवति तथा बहुधा भवान् एव प्रतीयते ॥१९॥ — Having perceived this universe created by Your own energies, such as passion and other substances, as the cause, You perceive Yourself in many ways as if You had not entered it, but remained within it as if it had entered it.
19.translation: If so, how can it be said that there is nothing perfected by direct perception and other things? O Brahman God. "Brahma" is the v text. Having perceived this universe created by Your own energies, such as passion and other substances, as the cause, You perceive Yourself in many ways as if You had not entered it, but remained within it as if it had entered it.

20.word_for_word: एकस्यैव बहुधा प्रतीतिं सदृष्टान्ताम् आह---यथा हीति । — He argues that the perception of the same thing in many ways is a good example: as follows.; योनिषु स्वस्यैव रूपान्तरेणाभिव्यक्ति-स्थानेषु चराचरेषु यथा मही-प्रमुखानि कारणान्य् एव नाना भान्ति । — There appear to be various causes, such as the earth, in the various places of expression in the various forms of the universe.; आत्म-योनिषु स्व-कारणेषु भूत-भौतिकेषु । — In the self-born, in the self-caused, in the physical and mental.; जीवोऽपि नर-मृगादि-शरीरेषु बाल-युवाद्य्-अवस्थासु च तथा तथा प्रतीयते इति तद् व्यवच्छेद् आर्थम् आत्म-तन्त्र-ग्रहणम् ॥२०॥ — The living entity also perceives himself in the same way in the bodies of men, animals and others, as well as in the states of childhood and youth.
20.translation: He argues that the perception of the same thing in many ways is a good example: as follows. There appear to be various causes, such as the earth, in the various places of expression in the various forms of the universe. In the self-born, in the self-caused, in the physical and mental. The living entity also perceives himself in the same way in the bodies of men, animals and others, as well as in the states of childhood and youth.

21.word_for_word: ननु सृष्ट्य्-आदि-कर्तृत्वेन च मम किं जीव-वद् बन्ध उक्तो न हि न हीत्य् आह---सृजसीति । — If, indeed, I am the doer of creation and the beginning, why is it said that I am bound like a living being?; तद्-गुण-कर्मभिर् वा तैर् गुणैः कर्मभिर् वेत्य् अर्थः । — That is, by the qualities and actions of those qualities or by the actions of those qualities.; यतः क्व च कदाचिद् अपि बन्ध-हेतुर् अविद्या तव नैवास्ति । — Because ignorance is not your cause of bondage anywhere and at any time.; कुत इत्य् अत आह---ज्ञानात्मन इति । — Where, then, he argues, is that of the Self of Knowledge?; मायाया आश्रयानावरकत्वाद् इति भावः ॥२१॥ — This means that it is the covering of the shelter of illusion.
21.translation: If, indeed, I am the doer of creation and the beginning, why is it said that I am bound like a living being? That is, by the qualities and actions of those qualities or by the actions of those qualities. Because ignorance is not your cause of bondage anywhere and at any time. Where, then, he argues, is that of the Self of Knowledge? This means that it is the covering of the shelter of illusion.

22.word_for_word: किं च आस्तां तावद् बन्ध-शङ्का, यतो विद्योपाधेर् जीवात्मनोऽपि न वस्तुतो बन्धोऽस्तीत्य् आह---देहाद्य्-उपाधेर् इति । — What is more, there is so much doubt about bondage, since even the soul of the living entity is not actually bound by the concept of knowledge, he argues, because of the concept of body and other things.; भवो जन्म तन् मूला भिदा च साक्षात् स्वरूपतो न स्याद् इति । — Being, birth, that root, and difference, cannot be directly inherent in nature.; ननु मम बन्धाभावं वदता त्वया किं मोक्षोऽङ्गी-क्रियते, ॐ इति चेत् तर्हि बन्धाभावे मोक्षासम्भवाद् आपन्नो बन्धोऽपीत्य् आशङ्क्याह---अत इति । — If, indeed, when you say that I am not bound, do you accept liberation?; यतो नाविद्या अतो न बन्धो मोक्षश् च । — Because there is no ignorance, there is no bondage and no liberation.; एवम् उभौ न स्याताम् इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that neither should be.; ननु उलूखले मां बद्धं श्रुतवान्, यमुना-ह्रदे मुक्तं च दृष्टवान् असि, अतः कथम् उभयं नास्त्य् अत आह---निकाम इति । — Indeed, you have heard me bound in a mortar and seen me freed in the lake of Yamuna. How can there be no both?; स्वाभिप्रायानुरूपस् त्वयि नोऽस्माकम् अविवेक एव परम् एवं-भूत इति । — It is our lack of discrimination against you that is in accordance with our own intentions.; यद्वा नोऽविवेक एव तवोभौ स्याताम् इति ॥२२॥ — Or else it is our indiscretion that both of you may be.
22.translation: What is more, there is so much doubt about bondage, since even the soul of the living entity is not actually bound by the concept of knowledge, he argues, because of the concept of body and other things. Being, birth, that root, and difference, cannot be directly inherent in nature. If, indeed, when you say that I am not bound, do you accept liberation? Because there is no ignorance, there is no bondage and no liberation. This means that neither should be. Indeed, you have heard me bound in a mortar and seen me freed in the lake of Yamuna. How can there be no both? It is our lack of discrimination against you that is in accordance with our own intentions. Or else it is our indiscretion that both of you may be.

23.word_for_word: ननु तर्हि ममावतारास् तच्-चरित्राणि च शुक्ति-रजत-वद् अविद्या-कल्पितान्य् एव किम् ? — Are My incarnations and their characters, then, imagined by ignorance like pure silver?; न हि न हि, इयं तु तव लीलेत्य् आह द्वयेन---त्वयोदित इति ॥२३॥ — "No, no, but this is your pastime," he said in two ways, "as you have said.
23.translation: Are My incarnations and their characters, then, imagined by ignorance like pure silver? "No, no, but this is your pastime," he said in two ways, "as you have said.

24.word_for_word: सुरेतरांशा ये राजानस् तेषाम् अक्षौहिणी-शतानां बधेन भूमेर् भारम् अपनेतुं स्वांशेन रामेन सहावतीर्णोऽसि ॥२४॥ — You have descended along with your own part Rama to relieve the burden of the earth by killing hundreds of akshauhini kings who are part of the gods
24.translation: You have descended along with your own part Rama to relieve the burden of the earth by killing hundreds of akshauhini kings who are part of the gods

25.word_for_word: अत एवं-भूतस्य तवागमनेन कृतार्थोऽस्मीत्य् आह त्रयेण, अद्येति । — Therefore, having thus-been, I am satisfied with your coming, he said, in three ways, today.; हे ईश, अद्य नो वसतयो गृहास् तपो-वनाद् अपि बहु-पुण्याः । — O Lord, today our dwellings are more pious than the forest of austerities.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; या वसतीस् त्वं साक्षात् प्रविष्टः । — You have entered the dwelling place directly.; कथं भूतः । — How did it happen?; यस्य तव पाद-सलिलम् एव गङ्गा त्रि-जगत् पुनाति, यश् च त्वं पञ्च-यज्ञ-देवता-मूर्तिः स त्वं जगद्-गुरुर् इति ॥२५॥ — The Ganges purifies the three worlds by the very waters of Thy feet, and Thou art the embodiment of the five sacrificial deities, and Thou art the spiritual master of the universe.
25.translation: Therefore, having thus-been, I am satisfied with your coming, he said, in three ways, today. O Lord, today our dwellings are more pious than the forest of austerities. Where is it from? You have entered the dwelling place directly. How did it happen? The Ganges purifies the three worlds by the very waters of Thy feet, and Thou art the embodiment of the five sacrificial deities, and Thou art the spiritual master of the universe.

26.word_for_word: स्व-मनोरथः परिपूरित इति तुष्यन्न् आह---कः पण्डित इति । — Satisfied that his wish had been fulfilled, he asked, "Who is a scholar?"; ऋत-गिरः सत्य-वाचः । — The truthful word is the truthful word.; त्वत्तोऽपरं शरणंकः समीयाद् गच्छेत् । — There is no other refuge than you.; यतो भवान् भजतः सर्वान् अभितः कामांश् च ददात्य् आत्मानम् अपीति ॥२६॥ — Because Thou givest all desires to those who worship Thee, even Thyself.
26.translation: Satisfied that his wish had been fulfilled, he asked, "Who is a scholar?" The truthful word is the truthful word. There is no other refuge than you. Because Thou givest all desires to those who worship Thee, even Thyself.

27.word_for_word: नोऽविवेकिनाम् । — Not for the irrational.; तत्रापीह गृह एव ॥२७॥ — Even there, it is a house.
27.translation: Not for the irrational. Even there, it is a house.

29.word_for_word: वो युष्माकं प्रजाः पुत्रा हि वयम् इति ॥२९॥ — You are your subjects and we are your sons.
29.translation: You are your subjects and we are your sons.

30.word_for_word: ननु नृभिर् देवाः सेव्या इति प्रसिद्धं तत्राह---देवा इति । — Indeed, it is well known that men should serve the gods.; स्वार्थाः स्व-कार्य-साधन-पराः, साधवस् तु केवलं परानुग्रह-पराः, परमार्थतस् तु साधव एव देवा इति त एव सेव्या इत्य् अर्थः ॥३०॥ — They are selfish and devoted to the means of their own work, but the saintly are devoted only to the mercy of others, and in the ultimate sense the saintly are the gods, this means that they alone should be served.
30.translation: Indeed, it is well known that men should serve the gods. They are selfish and devoted to the means of their own work, but the saintly are devoted only to the mercy of others, and in the ultimate sense the saintly are the gods, this means that they alone should be served.

31.word_for_word: तर्हि मृच्-छिलादि-मयाः किं देवादयो नैवेत्य् अत आह---न हीति । — Then why are not the gods and others made of clay, chila and other materials?; अम्मयानि तीर्थानि मृन्-मयाः शिला-मयाश् च देवा न भवन्तीति न, अपि तु भवन्त्य् एव । — It is not that the holy places made of water and the gods made of clay and stone do not exist, but they do exist.; तथापि साधूना तेषां च महद् अन्तरम् इत्य् आह---ते पुनन्तीति ॥३१॥ — Yet there is a great difference between the saintly and them, he argues, for they purify.
31.translation: Then why are not the gods and others made of clay, chila and other materials? It is not that the holy places made of water and the gods made of clay and stone do not exist, but they do exist. Yet there is a great difference between the saintly and them, he argues, for they purify.

32.word_for_word: किञ्चिच् चिकीर्षयन् प्रागात् इति यद् उक्तं तत् कार्यम् आदिशति, स इति । — He orders the action, which is said to be the action of the preceding, intending to do something, that is, he.; नः सुहृदां मध्ये भवान् श्रेष्ठोऽतः पाण्डवानां श्रेयश् चिकीर्षया गजाह्वयं गच्छस्व गच्छेति । — You are the best of our friends, so if you want to do the best for the Pāṇḍavas, go to Gajahvāya and go.; यद्वा स्वेति पृथक् पदम् । — or, Sweti, is a separate term.; हे स्व आत्मीयेत्य् अर्थः ॥३२॥ — O self-realized one, that is, O self-realized one.
32.translation: He orders the action, which is said to be the action of the preceding, intending to do something, that is, he. You are the best of our friends, so if you want to do the best for the Pāṇḍavas, go to Gajahvāya and go. or, Sweti, is a separate term. O self-realized one, that is, O self-realized one.

33.word_for_word: राज्ञा धृतराष्ट्रेण । — by King Dhritarashtra.; वसन्ते निवसन्ति । — They live in the spring.; शुश्रुम श्रुतवन्तो वयम् ॥३३॥ — We have heard and we have heard.
33.translation: by King Dhritarashtra. They live in the spring. We have heard and we have heard.

34.word_for_word: दुष्टा ये स्व-पुत्रा दुर्योधनादयस् तद्-वशेन गच्छतीति तथा । — He also goes under the control of his wicked sons, such as Duryodhana.; यतोऽन्ध-दृग् अन्ध-नेत्रः ॥३४॥ — Because the blind-eyed is blind-eyed.
34.translation: He also goes under the control of his wicked sons, such as Duryodhana. Because the blind-eyed is blind-eyed.
